analysis: The change to .github/workflows/release-provider.yml has two parts. At head line 112-114 it adds a workflow-level env DARKBLOOM_PROVIDER_TOOLCHAIN: release, with a comment that release bytes build, qualify and sign with Xcode 27.2 only (scripts/prepare-provider-release-toolchain.sh). At head line 1444 the older-macOS validation lane now asserts identity['build_sdk_version'] == '27.2' instead of '27.0'. Both are build-toolchain pinning and validation tightening. They add no secrets, permissions, triggers or untrusted-input interpolation, and the release gating is unchanged. Source verification via provider-release-resume.py verify-source runs before credentials, resolve-env checks out master, the signing job still uses the Developer ID and App Attest-relevant profile checks, and the publication artifact digest is still verified on download. The env var is workflow-level, so it reaches every job, including the secret-consuming ones. It is a static literal and does not alter trust decisions. It only selects the toolchain, which is a build-integrity improvement that narrows SDK drift. The 27.2 assertion compares against build_sdk_version from BUILD_SDK_VERSION, which build-and-release already checks equals $PROVIDER_SDK_VERSION at head line 453. A mismatch would fail the validation lane (fail-closed), not weaken it. Unverified: the contents of scripts/prepare-provider-release-toolchain.sh and whether PROVIDER_SDK_VERSION is actually 27.2, which are outside the supplied evidence. The next pass should confirm that the script enforces Xcode 27.2 and that the SDK version constant matches. This is relevant to the release-artifact trust chain (A-011, T-034), but no regression is visible here. The threat model entries retained for the provider mostly cover runtime behavior, so no model update is required for this CI toolchain pin.
